A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SymMPO study, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The earlier case-study appendix is retained as Appendix D in v2, alongside a new Appendix C.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, contrastive-image experiments, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds hyperparameter-sensitivity results in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: The symmetric pairwise objective, margin-consistency regularization, anchoring, CLIP-based image pairing, and caption-anchored data pipeline are retained. Explicit dataset expectations and parameter-selection explanations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both retain the VQA v2/MSCOCO/TextVQA training mixture, the same five evaluation benchmarks, and the same contrastive-image scenarios. The new parameter sweeps use existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator membership within each backbone setting, including the controlled DPO and mDPO comparisons. Figure 4 still compares SymMPO with mDPO; the new tables vary SymMPO settings only.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds reported LLaVA-1.5-7B sweep protocols: three learning rates, five lambda values, and four gamma values. The main evaluation metrics, backbone configurations, two-epoch training, batch size, and selected hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests sensitivity to learning rate, pairwise-loss weight lambda, and margin-regularization weight gamma. This focused extension supplements the retained component ablations, contrastive-image analysis, and case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run uncertainty for its experiments. The new sweep tables continue to report point estimates only.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 4 retain their results. Tables 3–5 add scores for different hyperparameter settings; for example, Table 3 reports MMStar scores of 28.2, 34.8, and 33.8 at learning rates 5e-5, 5e-6, and 5e-7. These supplement the unchanged main results.

T1.justification: Several losses now explicitly include dataset expectations, and Appendix B clarifies that its gradient calculation concerns individual training instances. The loss algebra, partition-function argument, and gradient derivations are otherwise retained; these are mathematical restatements rather than new theory.

C1.justification: The introduction corrects the evaluation claim from five hallucination benchmarks to four hallucination benchmarks plus one general image-question-answering benchmark. The conclusion similarly uses 'multimodal benchmarks.' The methodological contributions and superiority claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds an interpretation that excessively weak or strong margin regularization harms preference learning. Existing limitations are retained. Its statement that gamma is smaller than the learning rate conflicts with the reported values, 1e-4 and 5e-6.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code and data release; v2 states that code is available and supplies a repository link, without an equivalent data-release statement. Appendix C also documents search ranges, parameter selection, and the prior-work basis of the fixed beta, eta, and delta settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Stiennon et al. (2020), Ouyang et al. (2022), and Bradley and Terry (1952) to the background discussion. The related-work survey and positioning against existing multimodal preference methods are retained.

P1.justification: Section 2.1 is retitled and its RLHF introduction expanded. v2 adds the hyperparameter appendix and acknowledgments, renumbers the case-study appendix, and updates corresponding-author and conference information. Most scientific prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives revised backgrounds and borders, Figure 2 has a small illustrative-text edit, and Tables 3–5 are added. Existing tables and figures shift with pagination, while the main result displays and case-study figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity evidence and parameter-selection details in Appendix C improve transparency and support for the retained settings. Stated code access and corrected benchmark characterization also help. The erroneous comparison of gamma with the learning rate is a small drawback, outweighed by these limited gains; the main experimental evidence remains unchanged.
